newsitem.title: USA: Illinois corn 86 percent seeded vs 48 pct average.
newsitem.headline: Illinois corn 86 percent seeded vs 48 pct average.

text.p: Illinois farmers had planted 86 percent of the corn crop as of Sunday, well ahead of the five-year average of 48 percent, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.
Soybeans were 35 percent seeded, up from four percent last year and the five-year average of 12 percent.
While plantings were running ahead of average pace, cold and wet weather has stalled crop development.
"Emergence of corn has been slow," the report said. "Three to four weeks germination was quite common with emerged plants being yellowish color."
Oats were seven percent headed, against two percent average. The crop was rated 24 percent fair, 66 percent good, and 10 percent excellent.

Winter wheat was nine percent headed, against 17 percent for the five-year average. Wheat was rated two percent very poor, three percent poor, 21 percent fair, 63 percent good and 11 percent excellent.
Pasture was rated one percent very poor, three percent poor, 31 fair, 57 good and eight percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, five percent short, 76 percent adequate and 19 percent surplus.
